Q1475.t: Once the capital, now the most populous Philippine city
Q1475.s: For almost three decades this was the official capital of the Philippines, and today no Philippine city has more people. Quezon City fills the north-eastern side of Metro Manila, spread across a low plateau above the bay. At its northern edge a rare patch of dark green interrupts the grey: the forested watershed of the La Mesa reservoir, part of the capital region's water supply.
Q1475.w: The north-east corner of Metro Manila's grey sprawl, with a dark green forest and reservoir at its northern edge.
f: Quezon City was the official capital of the Philippines from 1948 to 1976, when Manila regained the title.
It is named after Manuel L. Quezon, president of the Philippine Commonwealth, who founded it in 1939.
The main campus of the University of the Philippines is in its Diliman district.

q.q: Who is Quezon City named after?

Q47916.t: Nawabs, kebabs and a looping river on the Ganges plain
Q47916.s: Follow the Gomti as it loops lazily across the flat Ganges plain, and you will find Lucknow wrapped around its bends. In 1775 the Nawabs of Awadh moved their capital here and filled it with domed imambaras, gardens and a court culture of poetry and fine manners. The city still trades on that refinement — and on its slow-cooked kebabs.
Q47916.w: A large city strung along the winding Gomti River on the flat, green Ganges plain.
f: Lucknow is famous for chikankari, a delicate white-on-white hand embroidery.
The Bara Imambara, built in the 1780s, hides a maze of narrow passages known as the Bhulbhulaiya.
Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state.

q.q: Which river winds through Lucknow?

Q173985.t: A colonial canal town that grew into a textile giant
Q173985.s: Until the late 19th century this was dry scrubland between the Chenab and Ravi rivers. Then British engineers dug irrigation canals, and in the 1890s a market town called Lyallpur rose among the new fields. At its centre stands a clock tower, with eight bazaars fanning out like the arms of a Union Jack. Renamed Faisalabad in 1977, it is now one of Pakistan's great textile centres.
Q173985.w: A big, flat city amid a chequerboard of irrigated fields, with straight canals running between two rivers.
f: Lyallpur was named after Sir James Lyall, a British lieutenant-governor of Punjab.
In 1977 the city was renamed in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.
The eight bazaars radiating from the clock tower were laid out to echo the British flag.

q.q: What was Faisalabad called before 1977?

Q61092.t: An island port tied to the mainland by two long bridges
Q61092.s: Two hair-thin lines stretch across the strait to Penang Island — road bridges of about 13 and 24 km. George Town fills the island's north-eastern cape, beneath a green, hilly interior. Francis Light founded it in 1786 as a British trading post, and its old quarter of shophouses, temples, mosques and clan houses is now a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Q61092.w: A small, hilly green island off Malaysia's west coast, a city on its north-east tip and two bridges to the mainland.
f: The second Penang bridge, opened in 2014, is about 24 km long.
George Town and Melaka were listed together as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2008.
Penang Hill rises above the city to more than 800 m; a funicular has climbed it since 1923.

q.q: Who founded George Town in 1786?

Q10392.t: Where Jakarta's sprawl rolls east without a seam
Q10392.s: Try to find where Jakarta ends and Bekasi begins — from cruise height you can't. The city merges into the capital's eastern flank, a grey carpet laced with toll roads, rail lines and the brown Bekasi River. Further east, the roofs of huge industrial estates glint, and beyond them green rice fields finally take over. Bekasi is the “Bek” in Jabodetabek, the name of Greater Jakarta.
Q10392.w: Grey sprawl merging with Jakarta's eastern edge, crossed by toll roads; factory roofs and rice fields farther east.
f: Jabodetabek stands for Jakarta, Bogor, Depok, Tangerang and Bekasi — one of the largest urban areas on Earth.
An elevated toll road about 36 km long runs above the Jakarta–Cikampek motorway through Bekasi.

q.q: Bekasi supplies the last syllable of which metro-area name?

Q66616.t: A plateau city famed for its night-time street food
Q66616.s: By day Sarafa is a jewellers' lane; after dark the shutters come down and food stalls move in, frying jalebis and kachoris until late. That switch sums up Indore, the largest city of Madhya Pradesh and a busy trading hub on the Malwa plateau. Around it, dark soil and flat fields stretch in every direction, broken by small reservoirs that glint in the sun.
Q66616.w: A large, compact city on a flat plateau of dark fields, dotted with small lakes and reservoirs.
f: Indore was the seat of the Holkar dynasty, whose Rajwada palace still stands in the old centre.
India's national cleanliness survey has ranked Indore the country's cleanest city many times.
The city stands at about 550 m on the Malwa plateau, above the Narmada valley to the south.

q.q: Which dynasty ruled from Indore?

Q72818.t: The Red River delta's seaport, framed by karst islands
Q72818.s: Brown delta rivers fan out into the Gulf of Tonkin here, and Haiphong grew up on one of them as northern Vietnam's main seaport. East of the city the flat delta breaks off at Cat Ba, an island of jagged limestone peaks next to Ha Long Bay. In early summer the streets blaze red with flamboyant trees, the flower that gave Haiphong its nickname.
Q72818.w: A port city among brown river mouths on a flat delta; jagged green limestone islands rise just to the east.
f: Cat Ba, the largest island in the Ha Long Bay area, belongs to Haiphong.
On the nearby Bạch Đằng River, Vietnamese forces twice trapped invading fleets on hidden stakes, in 938 and 1288.
A sea bridge about 5 km long links the city to the deep-water port of Lạch Huyện.

q.q: Haiphong's nickname comes from which red-flowering tree?

Q378879.t: A valley capital in the foothills of the Hindu Kush
Q378879.s: Snowy ridges crowd the horizon, and between them the green floor of the Swat valley opens like a corridor. Saidu Sharif and its twin town, Mingora, fill a bend of the valley beside the Swat River. The town grew around the shrine of a 19th-century saint, the Akhund of Swat, and until 1969 it was the capital of the princely state of Swat.
Q378879.w: Twin towns on a green valley floor beside a braided river, hemmed in by steep ridges that turn white in winter.
f: The town is named after Saidu Baba, the Akhund of Swat, whose shrine stands here.
Swat was a princely state until 1969, with Saidu Sharif as its capital.
The ruins of the Butkara Buddhist stupa, at the edge of town, are more than 2,000 years old.

q.q: Saidu Sharif was the capital of which princely state?

Q93230.t: The old bazaar city beside Pakistan's planned capital
Q93230.s: Two cities, one sprawl: Rawalpindi's dense, irregular streets run straight into the tidy grid of Islamabad to the north. Beyond, the wooded Margalla Hills form the first ridge of the Himalayan foothills, while to the south the Potohar plateau is cut by deep ravines. When Islamabad was chosen as the new capital in 1959, Rawalpindi stood in for it until the planned city was ready.
Q93230.w: A dense city merging into a neat grid to the north, below a wooded ridge; gullied plateau to the south.
f: Rawalpindi served as Pakistan's interim capital in the 1960s while Islamabad was being built.
The Grand Trunk Road, one of Asia's oldest highways, runs through the city.

q.q: Rawalpindi stood in as capital while which city was built?

Q11909.t: A princely city with crocodiles in its river
Q11909.s: A lone hill on the north-eastern horizon — Pavagadh, crowned with temples — is the landmark for finding Vadodara on the flat Gujarat plain. The Gaekwad maharajas made Baroda one of India's richest princely states and finished the vast Laxmi Vilas Palace here in 1890. Their river, the Vishwamitri, winds right through town, and it is still home to a large population of mugger crocodiles.
Q11909.w: A flat city on the Gujarat plain with a winding river through it; a lone steep hill rises about 45 km north-east.
f: Laxmi Vilas Palace is often said to be four times the size of Buckingham Palace.
Pavagadh hill and the ruined city of Champaner at its foot form a UNESCO World Heritage site.

q.q: Which reptile lives in large numbers in Vadodara's river?

Q200123.t: Punjab's workshop city in a sea of wheat and rice
Q200123.s: Around Ludhiana the land is ruled into squares of wheat in winter and rice in summer, some of the most intensively farmed fields in India. The city itself is the largest in Indian Punjab and its industrial engine, turning out bicycles, knitwear and machine parts. The Sutlej runs a few kilometres to the north, and one of its old channels, the Buddha Nullah, still threads through town.
Q200123.w: A large grey city on a flat plain of neat green or golden fields, with the broad Sutlej to the north.
f: Hero Cycles, founded in Ludhiana, grew into one of the world's largest bicycle makers.
Punjab Agricultural University in Ludhiana played a key role in India's Green Revolution of the 1960s.

q.q: Which product made Ludhiana's industry famous?

Q42941.t: The Taj Mahal's city, on a bend of the Yamuna
Q42941.s: The Yamuna swings in a wide bend here, and on its bank stands the reason millions come: the Taj Mahal, the white marble tomb Shah Jahan built for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Upstream, the red sandstone walls of Agra Fort follow the same river. From cruise height the monuments are too small to pick out, but the river's curve and the city packed along it are easy to find.
Q42941.w: A large city on the flat plain, wrapped around a sweeping bend of the Yamuna River south-east of Delhi.
f: The Taj Mahal took about 20 years to build; the whole complex was finished around 1653.
Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's red sandstone city about 35 km west, are World Heritage sites too.
Under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, Agra was for long periods the capital of the Mughal Empire.

q.q: Which river flows past the Taj Mahal?

Q366754.t: An ancient port on a winding creek east of Mumbai
Q366754.s: Follow the Ulhas River as it snakes west through mangroves towards Thane Creek, and Kalyan appears on its bank, merged with Dombivli into one dense suburb of Mumbai. Behind it, the flat-topped hills of the Western Ghats rise like a wall. Traders knew this port nearly two thousand years ago, and in the 17th century Shivaji built some of the first Maratha warships here.
Q366754.w: Dense suburbs along a winding, mangrove-lined river north-east of Mumbai, with the dark wall of the Western Ghats to the east.
f: At Kalyan Junction the main line from Mumbai splits, one branch climbing to Pune, the other to Nashik.
A 1st-century Greek sailing guide, the Periplus, mentions a port called Kalliena, identified with Kalyan.
Shivaji began building a Maratha fleet at Kalyan in the 1650s.

q.q: Which river flows past Kalyan?

Q243325.t: The last city before the Sundarbans mangroves
Q243325.s: South of Khulna the land dissolves into water: rivers split and rejoin, shrimp ponds glint like broken glass, and then a solid, dark green mass begins — the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest on Earth, home to Bengal tigers. Khulna, one of Bangladesh's largest cities, stands on the Rupsha and Bhairab rivers, and boats leave from here for the forest and the port of Mongla.
Q243325.w: A city on brown rivers in a flat delta of glinting ponds; the dark green Sundarbans mangroves begin to the south.
f: The Sundarbans continue across the border into India and are a UNESCO World Heritage site on both sides.
The Sixty Dome Mosque in nearby Bagerhat actually has more than sixty domes.

q.q: Which forest lies south of Khulna?

Q1800.t: A port of islands, backwaters and Chinese fishing nets
Q1800.s: Water and land interlock here like puzzle pieces: islands, peninsulas and lagoons edged with coconut palms, where the Kerala backwaters meet the Arabian Sea. Kochi has traded pepper and spices with the world for centuries. Chinese, Arab, Portuguese, Dutch and British merchants all left their mark, and cantilevered Chinese fishing nets still rise and dip along the shore of Fort Kochi.
Q1800.w: A city scattered over islands and peninsulas at a gap in the coast, with wide lagoons and palm-green land behind.
f: Vasco da Gama died in Kochi in 1524 and was first buried in St Francis Church.
In 2015 Kochi's airport became the first in the world to run entirely on solar power.
Willingdon Island, home to the port, was built in the 20th century from sand dredged out of the harbour.

q.q: Which explorer died in Kochi in 1524?

Q243322.t: Punjab's “city of wrestlers”, on the old trunk road
Q243322.s: Between Lahore and the Chenab River, Gujranwala stretches along the Grand Trunk Road across a flat, irrigated plain. It is proud of two things above all: its wrestlers — it is known as the City of Wrestlers — and its hearty food. Maharaja Ranjit Singh, who went on to build the Sikh Empire, was born here in 1780.
Q243322.w: A large, flat city along a straight highway north of Lahore, amid green irrigated fields; the Chenab lies to the north.
f: Ranjit Singh, born in Gujranwala, later made Lahore the capital of the Sikh Empire.
The city stands in the Rechna Doab, the fertile land between the Chenab and Ravi rivers.

q.q: Gujranwala is nicknamed the city of…?

Q200235.t: A sacred city near the source of the Godavari
Q200235.s: The Godavari, one of India's great rivers, is still young when it flows through Nashik: its source at Trimbakeshwar is only about 30 km away. Every twelve years the riverbanks fill with pilgrims for the Kumbh Mela. Around the city the basalt Western Ghats step down to the Deccan plateau, and the fields are lined with vineyards — Nashik is the centre of India's wine industry.
Q200235.w: A city on a small river at the foot of flat-topped basalt hills, with the Gangapur reservoir glinting to the west.
f: By legend, Lakshmana cut off the demoness Shurpanakha's nose here — nasika in Sanskrit — giving the city its name.
A government press in Nashik prints Indian rupee banknotes.

q.q: Which great river rises near Nashik?

Q200237.t: Where the great uprising of 1857 began
Q200237.s: On 10 May 1857, Indian soldiers of the East India Company's army rose up in the cantonment of Meerut and marched on Delhi, about 70 km away. It was the start of the largest revolt against British rule in that century. Today Meerut is a busy city on the flat land between the Ganges and the Yamuna, known for its sports goods — cricket bats and balls especially.
Q200237.w: A sizeable city on the flat, green plain between two rivers, north-east of Delhi's sprawl.
f: Hastinapur, the Kuru capital of the Mahabharata, is traditionally placed about 40 km north-east of Meerut.
Meerut is one of India's main centres for making cricket equipment.

q.q: In which year did the great uprising begin at Meerut?

Q200663.t: Delhi's industrial neighbour at the end of the Aravallis
Q200663.s: The last low ridges of the Aravalli Hills, one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, fade out on Faridabad's western side, while the Yamuna floodplain spreads to the east. Between them, the city runs south from Delhi in a long industrial strip. Sheikh Farid, a treasurer of the emperor Jahangir, founded it in 1607 to guard the highway, and it still carries his name.
Q200663.w: A long urban strip south of Delhi: rocky, scrubby hills to the west and the flat Yamuna floodplain to the east.
f: Every February the Surajkund crafts fair on the city's edge draws artisans from across India and abroad.
Surajkund itself is an ancient reservoir shaped like an amphitheatre, attributed to the 10th century.

q.q: Which crafts fair is held each February near Faridabad?

Q207098.t: Where Delhi spills east across the Yamuna
Q207098.s: Cross the Yamuna eastward out of Delhi and the city simply keeps going: Ghaziabad is where the capital's sprawl spills into Uttar Pradesh. The Hindon River runs through it, a thin line winding south to join the Yamuna. The city was founded in 1740 by the Mughal noble Ghazi-ud-Din, who called it Ghaziuddinnagar; the shorter name came later.
Q207098.w: Dense suburbs east of the Yamuna, merged with Delhi, with a small river winding south through them.
f: Ghaziabad Junction is one of the main rail gateways from Delhi towards eastern India.
It is often called the Gateway of Uttar Pradesh, since the main roads from Delhi into the state pass through it.

q.q: What was Ghaziabad originally called?

Q185518.t: Burma's last royal city, built around a moated square
Q185518.s: A perfect square about 2 km on each side, ringed by a moat that flashes silver in the sun, marks the heart of Mandalay: the walled grounds of the royal palace. King Mindon founded the city in 1857 beside the broad Irrawaddy, and it became the last royal capital of Burma. Mandalay Hill rises just to the north-east, its stairways lined with pagodas.
Q185518.w: A city beside the wide Irrawaddy with a huge moated square at its centre and a lone hill to the north-east.
f: Kuthodaw Pagoda holds 729 marble slabs carved with Buddhist scripture, often called the world's largest book.
The U Bein Bridge nearby, about 1.2 km of teak posts across a lake, is often called the longest teak bridge in the world.
Mandalay was the royal capital for less than 30 years, until the British took it in 1885.

q.q: Which king founded Mandalay in 1857?

Q200878.t: Where the Narmada cuts through cliffs of marble
Q200878.s: Just outside Jabalpur the Narmada squeezes into a gorge of white and grey marble a few kilometres long, then tumbles over the Dhuandhar Falls — the “smoke cascade”. Upstream the river is held back by the Bargi Dam, and the reservoir's long, branching arms spread across the forested hills south-west of the city. Jabalpur itself stands among rocky outcrops at the edge of the Narmada valley.
Q200878.w: A city among rocky hills near a large, many-armed reservoir to the south-west, with the Narmada winding past.
f: Boat rides through the Marble Rocks gorge at Bhedaghat are popular on moonlit nights, when the white cliffs glow.
The Narmada is one of the few large Indian rivers that flow west, into the Arabian Sea.

q.q: Which river cuts the Marble Rocks gorge near Jabalpur?

Q11854.t: Where young Gandhi went to school
Q11854.s: Before he was a lawyer, a campaigner or the Mahatma, Mohandas Gandhi was a schoolboy in Rajkot, where his father served as chief minister of the small princely state. The city spreads across the dry, flat Kathiawar peninsula, beside the Aji River and its reservoirs. Today Rajkot is one of Gujarat's biggest cities, known for its engineering workshops and gold jewellery.
Q11854.w: A large city on a dry, flat plain in western India, with small lakes and reservoirs around its edges.
f: Gandhi studied at Rajkot's Alfred High School, whose building is now a museum dedicated to him.
His father, Karamchand Gandhi, was diwan — chief minister — of the princely state of Rajkot.

q.q: Which future leader went to school in Rajkot?

Q244159.t: India's coal capital, pocked with open-cast mines
Q244159.s: Grey and black scars break up the green around Dhanbad: open-cast pits, spoil heaps and railway sidings of the Jharia coalfield, one of India's richest. Coal has been dug here since the late 19th century, and some seams have been burning underground for more than a hundred years. To the east, reservoirs on the Damodar and Barakar rivers add the only big patches of blue.
Q244159.w: Dark patches of open-cast mines and spoil heaps around a city, with large reservoirs on the rivers to the east.
f: Some coal seams under Jharia have been on fire since the early 20th century.
IIT (ISM) Dhanbad began in 1926 as the Indian School of Mines.

q.q: Dhanbad is nicknamed India's capital of what?

Q25563103.t: Capital of the Kakatiyas, ringed by old walls and lakes
Q25563103.s: Warangal's old fort was built in rings: the Kakatiya kings, who ruled from here in the 12th to 14th centuries, surrounded it with concentric walls of earth and stone. Their carved stone gateways still stand in an open field. The Kakatiyas were also master builders of irrigation tanks, and their lakes still glint among the rice fields of the Deccan all around.
Q25563103.w: A city on the Deccan plateau with lakes scattered around it and granite hills rising from the fields.
f: One of the fort's stone gateways, the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam, appears on Telangana's state emblem.
The Ramappa Temple, a Kakatiya masterpiece north-east of the city, became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2021.
The Thousand Pillar Temple in Hanamkonda was built by the Kakatiyas in the 12th century.

q.q: Which dynasty ruled from Warangal?

Q162442.t: Where two great rivers meet, and millions gather
Q162442.s: Here the muddy Ganges and the greener Yamuna meet, and on a clear day you can see the two colours run side by side before they blend. Hindus call this confluence the Triveni Sangam, adding a third, invisible river, the Saraswati. Allahabad, officially Prayagraj since 2018, hosts the Kumbh Mela, one of the largest gatherings of people on Earth.
Q162442.w: A city in the angle where two broad rivers merge; at its south-eastern tip, paler and darker waters meet.
f: Akbar built a fort right at the confluence in 1583 and named the city Ilahabad.
During the Kumbh Mela a temporary tent city rises on the sandy riverbanks.
The University of Allahabad, founded in 1887, is one of India's oldest modern universities.

q.q: Which two rivers meet at Allahabad?

Q170315.t: A pine-scented hill town that kept a British officer's name
Q170315.s: At more than 1,200 m, Abbottabad sits in a green bowl of pine-covered hills, cool enough to draw summer visitors from the hot Punjab plains. It was founded in 1853 by Major James Abbott, who wrote a poem of farewell to the town when he left. The Karakoram Highway passes through on its long climb north towards the Khunjerab Pass and China.
Q170315.w: A town in a green, bowl-shaped valley among forested hills, where the plains give way to mountains.
f: Abbottabad is a gateway to the Galyat hill resorts, such as Nathia Gali.
The Karakoram Highway runs from here towards the Khunjerab Pass, more than 4,600 m high.

q.q: Who is Abbottabad named after?

Q12478970.t: Java's southern harbour, sheltered by a long island
Q12478970.s: Java's south coast is mostly a wall of surf facing the Indian Ocean, which makes Cilacap unusual: a long, forested island, Nusa Kambangan, runs just offshore and shelters a natural harbour. Behind the island spreads Segara Anakan, a lagoon fringed with mangroves. On the mainland shore stand the tanks and chimneys of Indonesia's largest oil refinery.
Q12478970.w: A long, dark green island just off Java's south coast, a mangrove lagoon behind it and a port town at its eastern end.
f: The Cilacap refinery, run by Pertamina, is the largest in Indonesia.
The Segara Anakan lagoon is slowly shrinking as rivers fill it with silt.

q.q: Which long island shelters Cilacap's harbour?

Q170115.t: A lake city of houseboats in a ring of Himalayan peaks
Q170115.s: The Kashmir Valley is a flat green floor about 1,600 m up, walled in by snowy ranges, and Srinagar spreads across its middle. On its eastern edge lies Dal Lake, dotted with floating gardens and lined with carved wooden houseboats. The Jhelum River loops through the old city, while Mughal gardens climb in terraces up the hillsides above the lake.
Q170115.w: A city on a flat valley floor beside a large lake, with snowy ranges all around; the Jhelum winds through it.
f: Shalimar Bagh, laid out for the Mughal emperor Jahangir in the 1600s, is one of Dal Lake's terraced gardens.
Many of Dal Lake's vegetable gardens float on mats of reeds and soil.
Houseboats became popular in the 19th century, when outsiders were not allowed to own land in Kashmir.

q.q: Which lake, famous for houseboats, borders Srinagar?

Q200017.t: Where the Krishna leaves the hills for its delta
Q200017.s: Watch the Krishna River break through a line of low hills and spread onto the plain: Vijayawada stands right in that gap. A barrage more than a kilometre long stretches across the river here, and from it canals fan out to water the rice fields of the Krishna delta. On a hill beside the river stands the Kanaka Durga temple, one of the most visited in Andhra Pradesh.
Q200017.w: A city at a gap in low hills where a long barrage crosses a wide river, with canals fanning out into green fields.
f: The Prakasam Barrage, over 1 km long, was completed in 1957 on the site of a 19th-century dam.
The Undavalli cave temples, cut into a hillside across the river, date from around the 4th–5th centuries.

q.q: Which river does the Prakasam Barrage span?

Q1645.t: A river city of gold, rafts and pineapple fields
Q1645.s: The name promises gold, and there really was gold in the river that gave Cagayan de Oro its name. Today the same river is better known for whitewater rafting as it rushes down from the Bukidnon highlands into Macajalar Bay. Up on that plateau, vast pineapple plantations cover the land in geometric patches, while the city spreads along the bay on Mindanao's north coast.
Q1645.w: A city at a river mouth on a wide bay on Mindanao's north coast; a plateau of geometric plantations rises inland.
f: Its nickname is the City of Golden Friendship.
The pineapple plantations on the Bukidnon plateau are among the largest in the world.

q.q: What does “de Oro” mean in the city's name?

Q216075.t: Capital of the Mekong Delta, where markets float
Q216075.s: Green land sliced into thin strips by canals, brown water everywhere: this is the Mekong Delta, and Cần Thơ is its largest city. It stands on the Hậu River, the delta's southern main branch, which is well over a kilometre wide here. At dawn, boats laden with pineapples, melons and pumpkins gather at the Cái Răng floating market.
Q216075.w: A city on a very wide brown river amid a flat green delta, cut into strips by countless canals.
f: At Cái Răng, sellers hang their produce from a tall pole on the boat, so buyers can see from afar what is on offer.
The Hậu River is also known as the Bassac.

q.q: Which famous floating market is near Cần Thơ?

Q200713.t: Gateway to Ajanta and Ellora, with its own “Taj”
Q200713.s: Brown basalt hills and flat-topped ridges surround Aurangabad, and they hide some of India's greatest treasures. Ellora's rock-cut temples are about 30 km to the north-west, and the painted caves of Ajanta about 100 km to the north. The city itself has the Bibi Ka Maqbara, built in the 1660s for the wife of the emperor Aurangzeb and often called the Taj of the Deccan.
Q200713.w: A city in a basin of brown basalt hills; a conical fortress hill stands on its north-western outskirts.
f: Daulatabad fort, on a steep cone of rock nearby, briefly became the capital of the Delhi Sultanate in 1327.
Ajanta and Ellora have both been UNESCO World Heritage sites since 1983.

q.q: Which monument is called the “Taj of the Deccan”?

Q237847.t: A Deccan mill town of bedspreads and towels
Q237847.s: Solapur has been weaving since the days of the cotton mills, and its name still turns up on bedspreads and towels across India: Solapuri chaddars carry a protected geographical indication. The city spreads over dry, open Deccan country not far from the border with Karnataka. Near its centre, the white Siddheshwar temple stands on an island in a small lake.
Q237847.w: A flat city in dry, open plateau country, with a small lake near its centre and reservoirs on the plains around.
f: Solapur chaddars and Solapur terry towels both have geographical-indication status in India.
A sanctuary near Solapur protects the great Indian bustard, one of the heaviest flying birds in the world.

q.q: Solapur's weavers are famous for which item?

Q174461.t: A plateau capital of waterfalls and red earth
Q174461.s: At about 650 m on the Chota Nagpur Plateau, Ranchi is cooler and greener than the plains below, and its outskirts mix forest, red earth and rocky hills. Rivers tumble off the plateau edge in a string of waterfalls, which gave it the nickname City of Waterfalls. The capital of Jharkhand is also the hometown of the cricket captain MS Dhoni.
Q174461.w: A city on a rolling plateau of green forest and red soil, with several reservoirs close by.
f: Hundru Falls, where the Subarnarekha drops off the plateau, is nearly 100 m high.
The Subarnarekha River rises just outside Ranchi.
Ranchi became a state capital in 2000, when Jharkhand was created.

q.q: Which cricketer calls Ranchi home?

Q25282.t: A long white beach between a mountain pass and a peninsula
Q25282.s: Few coastlines are this easy to read: a long white beach curving south, a green, mountainous peninsula — Sơn Trà — hooking out to the north-east, and the Hải Vân range plunging into the sea to the north-west. Da Nang fills the bay between them, split by the Hàn River. South-east of the centre, five marble hills rise abruptly from the flat sand.
Q25282.w: A bay city with a green peninsula to the north-east, mountains dropping into the sea to the north-west and a long white beach southward.
f: The five Marble Mountains are named after the five elements: metal, water, wood, fire and earth.
Sơn Trà peninsula is home to red-shanked douc langurs, among the most colourful primates in the world.
The Hải Vân Pass has long been seen as a climate divide between northern and southern Vietnam.

q.q: How many hills make up Da Nang's Marble Mountains?

Q200019.t: The Blue City under a fortress cliff on the desert's edge
Q200019.s: Jodhpur's old town is painted in shades of blue, and above it Mehrangarh Fort rises straight out of a rocky ridge, about 120 m above the plain. From cruise height the blue fades into a pale city on the edge of the Thar Desert, but the rocky ridge and the lakes beside it are easy to spot. Rao Jodha founded the city in 1459 as the capital of Marwar.
Q200019.w: A pale city beside a dark rocky ridge on the eastern edge of the Thar Desert, with lakes to the west.
f: Jodhpur breeches, the riding trousers, take their name from the city.
Umaid Bhawan, finished in 1943, is one of the largest private homes in the world; part is still the royal residence.

q.q: Which riding garment is named after the city?

Q199605.t: Gateway to the Northeast on the mighty Brahmaputra
Q199605.s: Elsewhere in Assam the Brahmaputra sprawls across its valley in braided channels many kilometres wide, but at Guwahati hills squeeze it into a single channel little more than a kilometre across. That narrow point made the city the natural crossing and gateway to India's Northeast. On the south bank, Nilachal Hill carries the Kamakhya temple, one of the most revered Hindu shrines.
Q199605.w: A city stretched along the south bank of a huge river, where green hills pinch it into one channel.
f: In 1671 an Ahom fleet defeated a Mughal army on the river here, at the Battle of Saraighat.
Umananda, in mid-river, is often called one of the world's smallest inhabited river islands.
The first bridge across the Brahmaputra, at Saraighat, opened here in 1962.

q.q: Which river flows past Guwahati?

Q43433.t: Le Corbusier's grid city at the foot of the Shivaliks
Q43433.s: Chandigarh is one of the few cities whose plan you can read from cruise altitude: a neat grid of rectangular sectors, laid out in the 1950s by Le Corbusier. The Shivalik foothills rise along its north-eastern edge, and an artificial reservoir, Sukhna Lake, fills the top corner. The city serves as the shared capital of two states, Punjab and Haryana.
Q43433.w: A regular grid of rectangular blocks at the foot of forested hills, with a lake at its north-eastern corner.
f: Each sector is roughly 800 by 1,200 m and was designed to be self-contained, with shops, schools and green space.
The Capitol Complex is part of a UNESCO site that groups Le Corbusier's buildings on three continents.
Nek Chand's Rock Garden is built from waste such as broken tiles, bottles and electrical sockets.

q.q: Which architect planned Chandigarh?

Q158467.t: A fortress on a sandstone mesa, and an early zero
Q158467.s: A long, flat-topped sandstone hill rises straight out of the middle of Gwalior, about 3 km long and crowned with the walls of one of India's most famous forts. The Mughal emperor Babur called it the pearl among the fortresses of Hind. Inside stands a small 9th-century temple with one of the oldest known inscriptions that writes zero as a digit.
Q158467.w: A long, narrow, flat-topped hill in the middle of a city on the plain; the Chambal ravines lie to the north.
f: The inscription in the Chaturbhuj temple, dated 876, writes the number 270 with a round zero.
Tansen, the legendary musician of Akbar's court, is buried in Gwalior, and a music festival is held at his tomb.
Jai Vilas Palace, still the home of the Scindia family, was built in the 1870s.

q.q: Which great musician of Akbar's court is buried in Gwalior?

Q167715.t: Kerala's capital near India's southern tip
Q167715.s: Almost at the tip of India, the coast here is a long line of surf, palm groves and small lagoons, with the Western Ghats rising blue-green inland. Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala's capital, grew around the Padmanabhaswamy temple and shares its name: the city of Lord Ananta, the serpent on which Vishnu rests. The airport runway runs almost parallel to the beach.
Q167715.w: A green, palm-covered city on a straight, surf-lined coast, with lagoons nearby and mountains rising to the east.
f: In 2011 vaults beneath the Padmanabhaswamy temple were found to hold a vast hoard of gold and jewels.
Kanyakumari, India's southern tip, is less than 100 km to the south-east.
The deep-water port of Vizhinjam, just south of the city, lies close to a major east–west shipping lane.

q.q: Which temple's vaults revealed a vast treasure in 2011?

Q207754.t: A rock, a river island and a colossal temple town
Q207754.s: Here the Kaveri divides into two broad, sandy channels, and between them stretches a long island, Srirangam — a shape you can trace from cruise height. On the island stands the Ranganathaswamy temple, one of the largest working Hindu temple complexes in the world, enclosed by seven concentric walls. Across the river, the Rockfort crag rises about 80 m above the old town of Tiruchirappalli.
Q207754.w: Two broad, sandy river channels running side by side with a long island between them; the city lies on the south bank.
f: The Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, downstream, is credited to the Chola king Karikala and is among the oldest water works still in use.
More than 400 rock-cut steps lead to the Ucchi Pillayar temple on top of the Rockfort.

q.q: What is the long river island at Tiruchirappalli called?

Q594275.t: The Philippines' tuna capital, under a lone volcano
Q594275.s: Every morning, tuna as long as a person are laid out in rows on the wet floor of the fish port — General Santos is the tuna capital of the Philippines. The city spreads around the head of Sarangani Bay on Mindanao's south coast. To the north rises Mount Matutum, a symmetrical, forested volcanic cone and a landmark for sailors and passengers alike.
Q594275.w: A city at the head of a wide bay on Mindanao's south coast, with a lone forested volcanic cone to the north.
f: The city is named after Paulino Santos, a general who led settlers here in 1939.
Mount Matutum is about 2,290 m high, and pineapple plantations cover its lower slopes.

q.q: General Santos is the Philippine capital of which fish?

ne-pp-1159150013.t: A Deccan twin city where India's flags are sewn
ne-pp-1159150013.s: Hubballi and its twin, Dharwad, about 20 km apart, together form one of Karnataka's largest urban areas, set in rolling black-soil country on the Deccan. For centuries this has been a market for cotton and grain. One local workshop has a special job: it is the only unit in India certified to make the national flags that fly over official buildings.
ne-pp-1159150013.w: A city on rolling plateau farmland of dark soil, with a smaller twin city about 20 km to the north-west.
f: The khadi flag unit at Bengeri in Hubballi is India's only flag maker certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards.
Hubballi is the headquarters of Indian Railways' South Western zone.

q.q: What is made in a Hubballi workshop for all of India?

Q10086.t: A palace city at the foot of Chamundi Hill
Q10086.s: A single hill, Chamundi, rises to about 1,060 m on the south-eastern edge of Mysuru, and the tidy city spreads out from its foot. North-west of town, the Krishna Raja Sagara reservoir fills a wide basin behind its dam. For centuries this was the seat of the Wodeyar kings, and during the Dasara festival their palace is lit up by nearly 100,000 bulbs.
Q10086.w: A neat city on a plateau beside a lone hill to the south-east, with a big reservoir about 15 km north-west.
f: Mysore silk, sandalwood carving and the sweet Mysore pak all take their name from the city.
Below the Krishna Raja Sagara dam on the Kaveri, completed in the 1930s, lie the terraced Brindavan Gardens.

q.q: Which festival is Mysuru's palace most famously lit up for?

Q372773.t: A capital of ponds and paddies in central India
Q372773.s: Flat paddy fields spread to the horizon around Raipur, and the land glints with countless small ponds and tanks, dug over centuries to store the monsoon rain. The city became the capital of Chhattisgarh when the state was created in 2000. South-east of the old centre, a new planned capital, Nava Raipur, has been laid out with a grid of broad avenues and artificial lakes.
Q372773.w: A city on a vast flat plain of rice fields dotted with ponds; a planned grid of avenues lies to the south-east.
f: Chhattisgarh is often called the rice bowl of India.
Raipur is one of the big centres of India's steel industry.

q.q: Chhattisgarh, with Raipur as capital, is called the bowl of…?

Q9863.t: A city in a ring of hills, known for its mangoes
Q9863.s: Hills close in on Salem from almost every side, and the city fills the valley floor between them. To the north the Shevaroy Hills rise steeply to a forested plateau, with the hill station of Yercaud on top at about 1,500 m. Salem is famous across India for its mangoes, and the district is the country's main centre for making sago from cassava.
Q9863.w: A city in a valley ringed by hills, with a steep, forested plateau rising directly to the north.
f: The Mettur Dam on the Kaveri, about 50 km west, holds back one of the largest reservoirs in Tamil Nadu.
The hills around Salem hold magnesite and iron ore, and a local plant rolls stainless steel.

q.q: Which hill station sits on the plateau above Salem?

Q8156.t: Sumatra's southern city, climbing hills above a bay
Q8156.s: At Sumatra's southern end, Bandar Lampung climbs green hills around the head of Lampung Bay, which opens south towards the Sunda Strait and Java. Some 75 km to the south, out in the strait, lies Krakatau, where a young cone, Anak Krakatau, rose from the sea in 1927. The city itself was formed by joining two towns: the port of Teluk Betung and upland Tanjung Karang.
Q8156.w: A hilly city wrapped around the head of a wide bay at Sumatra's southern tip, with islands scattered towards the bay's mouth.
f: Anak Krakatau — “child of Krakatau” — first rose above the sea in 1927.
Lampung province is one of Indonesia's leading coffee growers, mostly of robusta.
Way Kambas National Park, east of the city, runs a well-known centre for Sumatran elephants.

q.q: Tanjung Karang joined which port town to form Bandar Lampung?

Q33377.t: Punjab's sports-goods city between two rivers
Q33377.s: Between the Beas and the Sutlej lies the Doaba, the “land of two waters”, and Jalandhar is its biggest city. The plain around it is a patchwork of wheat, rice and potato fields, laced with canals. In its workshops, hockey sticks, cricket balls and footballs are made for players across India and far beyond.
Q33377.w: A large, flat city on an intensely farmed plain between two rivers, with canals running across the fields.
f: Doaba means “two waters”, after the Beas and the Sutlej, which enclose the region.
Sansarpur, a village on Jalandhar's edge, has produced more than a dozen Olympic hockey players.

q.q: Jalandhar's workshops are best known for making what?

Q330531.t: A Chambal river city of stone, saris and students
Q330531.s: The Chambal flows through Kota in a deep, rocky channel, and just upstream it has carved gorges into the edge of a plateau. A barrage holds the river back in the city, feeding canals that turn the dry plain green. Kota is known for three very different things: polished limestone, fine checked Kota Doria saris, and coaching schools where students from all over India prepare for exams.
Q330531.w: A city on both banks of a river in a rocky channel, with a barrage and green, canal-fed fields spreading out.
f: Kota stone, a hard, fine-grained limestone, is used for floors all over India.
Downstream, the Chambal is protected as a sanctuary for gharials, slender-snouted crocodiles.

q.q: Which river flows through Kota?

Q322155.t: Silk, mangoes and the wide sandbars of the Padma
Q322155.s: The Ganges, called the Padma here, spreads into a broad, braided channel of pale sandbars and shifting islands along Rajshahi's southern edge — a striking band of sand and water. The city is nicknamed the Silk City for its soft Rajshahi silk, and the orchards around it grow some of Bangladesh's most prized mangoes. It is also home to the country's oldest museum.
Q322155.w: A city on the north bank of a very wide river channel full of pale sandbars and islands.
f: The Varendra Research Museum, opened in 1910, is the oldest museum in Bangladesh.
Rajshahi silk, spun by mulberry silkworms, is famous for its saris.

q.q: What is the Ganges called where it flows past Rajshahi?

Q201832.t: A university town and India's city of locks
Q201832.s: In 1875 the reformer Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded a college here on the model of Oxford and Cambridge, and it grew into Aligarh Muslim University, whose campus fills a large part of the city. Aligarh is also India's lock city: its small workshops have turned out padlocks for generations. Around it, the flat plain between the Ganges and the Yamuna spreads in a patchwork of fields.
Q201832.w: A mid-sized city on the flat plain between the Ganges and Yamuna, amid a patchwork of green and brown fields.
f: Aligarh is nicknamed Tala Nagri, “the city of locks”.
The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q.q: Who founded the college that became Aligarh Muslim University?

Q11445.t: A cool upland city in a ring of volcanoes
Q11445.s: Count the volcanoes: Arjuno-Welirang to the north-west, Kawi to the west, the Tengger massif with Bromo to the north-east and, to the east, Semeru, the highest peak on Java at 3,676 m. Malang fills the high basin between them, about 450 m up — cool enough that Dutch planters built villas and tree-lined avenues here.
Q11445.w: A city in a green upland basin ringed by volcanoes; the tallest cone, often trailing ash, rises to the east.
f: Semeru is one of Java's most active volcanoes and often sends up small puffs of ash.
Neighbouring Batu, higher up the slopes, is known for its apple orchards.

q.q: Which volcano, Java's highest, rises east of Malang?

Q255455.t: The city of temples where the plains meet the hills
Q255455.s: The flat Punjab plain ends abruptly here: Jammu is built on the first low ridges of the Shivaliks, with the Tawi River cutting past in a wide, stony bed. Behind, range after range climbs north towards the snowy Pir Panjal. Its many shrines earned it the name City of Temples, and every year pilgrims pass through on their way to the Vaishno Devi cave shrine in the hills to the north.
Q255455.w: A city on low ridges where the flat plain meets the hills, split by a wide, stony riverbed; higher ranges rise north.
f: The Raghunath Temple, completed in the 1860s, is the best known of Jammu's many shrines.
The Vaishno Devi cave shrine, reached on foot from Katra, draws millions of pilgrims a year.

q.q: Which river flows through Jammu?

Q330643.t: India's brass city on the Ramganga
Q330643.s: Moradabad — or Muradabad, the city of Murad — was founded in 1625 on the Ramganga and named after the Mughal prince Murad Bakhsh. Today it is known as Peetal Nagri, the brass city: thousands of workshops hammer, engrave and polish brassware that is shipped all over the world. Around it the Ganges plain is flat and green, and the Himalayan foothills begin about 100 km to the north.
Q330643.w: A large city beside a winding river on the flat, green Ganges plain; the Himalayan foothills lie about 100 km north.
f: The city was founded in 1625 by Rustam Khan, a Mughal governor.
The Ramganga rises in the Kumaon Himalaya and joins the Ganges further south.

q.q: Moradabad is known as the city of which metal?

Q127041.t: Two rivers, a sandspit and the home of red roof tiles
Q127041.s: Two rivers, the Netravati and the Gurupura, curl around Mangalore and meet behind a long sandspit before slipping into the Arabian Sea. The city spreads over low laterite hills, green with coconut palms and cashew trees. Its name comes from the Mangaladevi temple, and it gave India the Mangalore tile — the red clay roof tile first made here in the 1860s.
Q127041.w: A coastal city on green hills where two rivers meet behind a sandspit; the Western Ghats rise inland.
f: The first Mangalore tile factory was set up in 1865 by the Basel Mission, a Swiss-German missionary society.
New Mangalore Port, north of the city, is the main seaport of the state of Karnataka.

q.q: Which building material is Mangalore famous for?

Q1629.t: Asia's Latin City, at the tip of Mindanao
Q1629.s: At the western tip of Mindanao, where the Sulu and Celebes seas meet, people speak Chavacano, a creole built largely on Spanish — the reason Zamboanga calls itself Asia's Latin City. The Spanish built Fort Pilar here in 1635. Offshore, Santa Cruz Island has a beach tinted pink by fragments of red organ-pipe coral, and bright-sailed vinta boats still cross the bay.
Q1629.w: A city spread along the southern tip of a long peninsula, facing a strait with islands offshore.
f: Fort Pilar, built by the Spanish in 1635, is now also a shrine and a museum.
Zamboanga is known as the sardine capital of the Philippines.

q.q: Which Spanish-based creole is spoken in Zamboanga?

Q185458.t: A fortress valley ringed by bare, folded mountains
Q185458.s: Bare brown ridges fold around Quetta on every side, their rock layers bent into stripes you can follow from cruise height. The city fills a high, flat valley at about 1,680 m, and its name is usually traced to a Pashto word for a fort. Irrigated orchards give it the nickname Fruit Garden of Pakistan, with apples, apricots, grapes and cherries grown around town.
Q185458.w: A city on a flat valley floor surrounded by bare, sharply folded brown mountains, with green orchards on its edges.
f: The Bolan Pass, a historic route between the Indus plain and the highlands, begins south-east of Quetta.
Mountains around Quetta, such as Takatu and Chiltan, rise to more than 3,000 m.

q.q: The name “Quetta” is usually traced to a word meaning…?

Q209698.t: A city of sandals, wrestlers and fiery curries
Q209698.s: Five streams join near Kolhapur to form the Panchganga — “five rivers” — which loops past the old city at the foot of the Sahyadri hills. Kolhapur gave its name to Kolhapuri chappals, hand-made leather sandals, and to a fiery style of mutton curry. The city also loves wrestling, and its traditional clay-pit gyms, the talims, still train champions.
Q209698.w: A city beside a looping river at the foot of forested Sahyadri hills, with a large lake near its centre.
f: The Mahalakshmi temple, one of the revered Shakti shrines, has drawn pilgrims to Kolhapur for centuries.
Panhala Fort, one of the largest hill forts in the Deccan, stands about 20 km north-west.

q.q: What does the name of Kolhapur's river, Panchganga, mean?

Q487656.t: Babur's birthplace at the far end of the Fergana Valley
Q487656.s: Mountains close in on three sides, and between them the Fergana Valley narrows to its eastern end — a dense green carpet of cotton fields, orchards and irrigation canals, with Andijan in the middle. In 1483 this was the birthplace of Babur, who would found the Mughal Empire in India. As a boy he inherited Fergana; he ended up conquering Delhi.
Q487656.w: A city in a densely farmed green valley, with mountains rising on three sides and a reservoir to the east.
f: Babur's memoir, the Baburnama, opens with a description of the Fergana Valley and Andijan.
Andijan region is home to Uzbekistan's main car factory, in the town of Asaka.

q.q: Which empire's founder was born in Andijan?

Q855122.t: A Sikh pilgrimage city on the banks of the Godavari
Q855122.s: The Godavari, a broad river by now after its long run across the Deccan, curves past Nanded in the Marathwada plains. The city is one of the holiest places in Sikhism: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, spent his last days here in 1708, and the gleaming Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib stands where he was cremated. Pilgrims come from Punjab, more than 1,000 km away.
Q855122.w: A city on the banks of a broad, winding river in the flat, farmed Marathwada plains.
f: Hazur Sahib is one of the five Takhts, the seats of authority in Sikhism.
At Nanded, Guru Gobind Singh declared the Sikh scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, to be the eternal Guru.

q.q: Which Sikh Guru spent his last days in Nanded?

Q207324.t: A thousand-year-old city on a spit between two rivers
Q207324.s: Cuttack is squeezed onto a narrow spit of land where the Mahanadi splits, with the main river on one side and its branch, the Kathajodi, on the other — two wide, sandy channels that are easy to see from cruise height. The city was Odisha's capital until 1948, when the government moved to nearby Bhubaneswar. Its silversmiths are famous for tarakasi, silver filigree as fine as lace.
Q207324.w: A city on a spit of land between two broad, sandy river channels, near the head of the Mahanadi delta.
f: Cuttack is often called the Millennium City, as its history goes back more than a thousand years.
During Durga Puja, Cuttack's images of the goddess are decorated with silver filigree.

q.q: Cuttack's silversmiths are famous for which craft?

Q220445.t: Borneo's “cat city” on a winding brown river
Q220445.s: A brown river loops through green lowland on its way to the South China Sea, and Kuching lines both of its banks. For about a century from 1841, the Brooke family ruled Sarawak from here as the “White Rajahs”. To the north, the lone peak of Mount Santubong rises from the coast, and nearby Bako National Park shelters proboscis monkeys.
Q220445.w: A city on both banks of a looping brown river in green lowlands; a lone coastal peak rises to the north.
f: Kuching's name is often linked to kucing, Malay for “cat”, and the city plays along with cat statues and a cat museum.
The Astana, the Brooke family's palace, stands on the north bank facing the waterfront.
Mount Santubong, about 810 m high, rises almost straight out of the sea.

q.q: Which family, the “White Rajahs”, ruled Sarawak from Kuching?

Q4803.t: A royal city of batik on Java's longest river
Q4803.s: Volcanoes frame Surakarta: Merapi and Merbabu to the west, Lawu to the east, with the city on the flat plain between them. Java's longest river, the Bengawan Solo, curves along its eastern edge. Better known simply as Solo, the city still has two royal courts, the Kasunanan and the Mangkunegaran, and it is one of the great centres of Javanese batik and gamelan music.
Q4803.w: A large city on a flat plain between volcanoes, with a river curving along its eastern side.
f: The Bengawan Solo, about 550 km long, is the longest river on Java.
A song called “Bengawan Solo”, written in 1940, became a hit across Asia.

q.q: Which river, Java's longest, flows past Surakarta?

Q140075.t: A wall of towers along an endless surf beach
Q140075.s: A straight line of surf runs for tens of kilometres, and right behind it stands a thin wall of high-rises — Surfers Paradise and its neighbours. Behind the towers, the land dissolves into a maze of man-made canals and islands, then a broad lagoon, the Broadwater. Inland, the forested ranges of the Gondwana Rainforests rise along the border with New South Wales.
Q140075.w: A long, straight beach backed by a thin line of towers, with a maze of canals and a lagoon behind and forested ranges inland.
f: The Gold Coast hosted the Commonwealth Games in 2018.
Lamington and Springbrook national parks in the hinterland are part of the Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage site.
In summer, clocks differ by an hour across the border at Coolangatta: New South Wales uses daylight saving, Queensland does not.

q.q: Which multi-sport event did the Gold Coast host in 2018?

Q5779.t: Sumatra's northern tip, the old “Veranda of Mecca”
Q5779.s: At the very northern tip of Sumatra, where the Aceh River meets the sea, Banda Aceh looks out over the Indian Ocean and the Andaman Sea. For centuries it was the capital of the Aceh Sultanate, and ships carrying pilgrims to Mecca set sail from here — which is why Aceh is still called the Veranda of Mecca. To the north lies Weh Island, Indonesia's traditional “kilometre zero”.
Q5779.w: A flat coastal city at Sumatra's northern tip, green mountains behind it and a hilly island offshore to the north.
f: The Baiturrahman Grand Mosque, with black domes and white walls, is the city's landmark.
In the early 17th century the Aceh Sultanate was one of the strongest powers in the region.

q.q: What is Aceh's traditional nickname?

Q213014.t: A cotton town of the Deccan, near a meteorite lake
Q213014.s: About 100 km south-west of Akola, a near-perfect circle of water sits in the flat basalt plateau: Lonar Lake, filling a crater blasted out by a meteorite. Akola itself is a market town of the Vidarbha region, set among black-soil cotton fields on the banks of the Morna River. It is also home to one of Maharashtra's agricultural universities.
Q213014.w: A town on a flat plain of dark cotton fields; a small, perfectly round crater lake lies about 100 km south-west.
f: Lonar crater, about 1.8 km across, is one of the few known meteorite craters formed in basalt.
Vidarbha's black soil, formed from weathered basalt, is ideal for growing cotton.

q.q: Akola lies in which cotton-growing region of Maharashtra?

Q242895.t: A wood-carvers' city beneath the Shivalik hills
Q242895.s: North of Saharanpur, the flat, fertile plain between the Ganges and the Yamuna runs into the first wooded ridges of the Shivaliks, the outermost range of the Himalaya. The city has been known for generations for its wood carving: craftsmen turn sheesham wood into intricately carved furniture, screens and boxes sold all over the world. Beyond the hills lies the Doon Valley and Dehradun.
Q242895.w: A city on a green plain just south of a line of low, wooded hills; the Yamuna runs to the west.
f: Saharanpur's wood carving has geographical-indication status in India.
The Eastern Yamuna Canal, one of India's oldest irrigation canals, runs through the district.

q.q: Which hills rise just north of Saharanpur?

Q37112.t: The first Bahmani capital, with a mosque under domes
Q37112.s: In 1347 the Bahmani Sultanate, the first great independent kingdom of the Deccan, made Gulbarga — officially Kalaburagi today — its capital. Inside the old fort stands its Jama Masjid, unusual in India because almost its entire prayer space is roofed with domes instead of an open courtyard. The dry plateau around the city grows pigeon peas, and Kalaburagi toor dal is famous across Karnataka.
Q37112.w: A city on a dry, flat plateau of brown and green fields, with small reservoirs and an old fort near its centre.
f: The fort's Jama Masjid, built in 1367, is often compared to the Great Mosque of Córdoba.
Kalaburagi toor dal, a split pigeon pea, has geographical-indication status.
The shrine of the Sufi saint Khwaja Bande Nawaz draws pilgrims of many faiths.

q.q: Which sultanate first made Gulbarga its capital?

Q45313.t: An ancient oasis city on the Hari River
Q45313.s: Green fields and orchards follow the Hari River across an otherwise dry, brown valley, and Herat stands in the middle of this oasis, with bare mountains to the north. It has been a crossroads for more than two thousand years. In the 15th century, as the Timurid capital, it became a centre of Persian poetry, miniature painting and architecture, and its Friday Mosque still glitters with blue tilework.
Q45313.w: A green oasis strung along a river in a dry, brown valley, with bare mountain ridges rising to the north.
f: The poet Jami and the painter Behzad both worked in Timurid Herat.
The citadel in the centre, Qala Ikhtiyaruddin, is traditionally said to go back to Alexander the Great.
Herat is known for its blue glass, still blown by hand in small workshops.

q.q: Which dynasty made Herat its capital in the 15th century?

Q485496.t: Kazakhstan's southern metropolis at the mountains' foot
Q485496.s: Snowy peaks of the Western Tien Shan line the south-eastern horizon, and below them Shymkent spreads over rolling foothills, green with parks and orchards. It is Kazakhstan's third-largest city. On its eastern edge stands ancient Sayram, a Silk Road town far older than Shymkent itself. To the west, beyond the Syr Darya, the sands of the Kyzylkum begin.
Q485496.w: A large city on green foothills, with snow-capped ranges to the south-east and dry steppe spreading west.
f: Aksu-Zhabagly, in the mountains to the east, was set up in 1926 as the first nature reserve in Central Asia.
Since 2018 Shymkent has been a city of republican significance, like Almaty and Astana.

q.q: Which ancient town now lies on Shymkent's eastern edge?

Q130469.t: A city grown around a blue-tiled shrine and white doves
Q130469.s: The flat plain of northern Afghanistan stretches from the foot of the Hindu Kush towards the Amu Darya, and Mazar-i-Sharif is its largest city. At its heart stands the Blue Mosque, a shrine covered in turquoise and cobalt tiles and famous for the flocks of white doves that live around it. About 20 km to the west lie the ruins of Balkh, one of the oldest cities in Central Asia.
Q130469.w: A city on a flat plain between bare mountains to the south and the Amu Darya valley to the north.
f: The name Mazar-i-Sharif is usually translated as “noble shrine”.
Ancient Balkh, known to the Greeks as Bactra, was called the Mother of Cities.
At Nowruz, the Persian new year, a great banner is raised at the shrine.

q.q: What does the name Mazar-i-Sharif mean?

Q1822.s: At around 1,500 m in the Cordillera, Baguio stays cool while Manila swelters, which is why American officials made it the country's summer capital in the early 1900s. Pine forests cover the ridges around the city, and the planner Daniel Burnham laid out its central park and streets. The city drapes itself over a knot of steep green ridges, with zigzag roads climbing to it from the lowlands.
Q1822.w: A city spread over steep, pine-covered ridges high in the mountains of northern Luzon, with zigzag roads climbing to it.
f: Burnham Park, at the city's heart, is named after Daniel Burnham, the Chicago planner who drew up Baguio's plan.
Neighbouring La Trinidad is famous for its strawberry farms.

q.q: Which American planner designed Baguio's layout?

Q14492.t: Borneo's oil town on a long, deep bay
Q14492.s: A long, deep bay cuts into the east coast of Borneo here, and on its shore the tanks and flares of a big refinery mark Balikpapan. The city grew from a fishing village after oil was struck in 1897, and it is still one of Indonesia's main oil and gas hubs. Its hilly streets face the Makassar Strait, while dense green forest and plantations spread inland.
Q14492.w: A hilly coastal city beside a long, narrow bay on Borneo's east coast, with an industrial shoreline and green hills inland.
f: The first oil well, drilled in February 1897, was named Mathilda.
Proboscis monkeys live in the mangroves of Balikpapan Bay.

q.q: Which strait does Balikpapan face?

Q52028.t: Old Lanna capital below the wooded wall of Doi Suthep
Q52028.s: Right at the western edge of Chiang Mai, a mountain wall rises straight from the Ping valley: Doi Suthep, almost 1,700 m high, with a gilded temple on its shoulder. The old city is a square about 1.5 km across, still ringed by a moat. King Mangrai founded Chiang Mai in 1296 as the capital of the Lanna kingdom, and its name means “new city”.
Q52028.w: A city on a flat valley floor with a river on its east side and a steep, forested mountain right at its western edge.
f: During the Yi Peng festival, thousands of paper lanterns are released into the night sky.
Doi Inthanon, Thailand's highest mountain at about 2,565 m, is about 60 km south-west.

q.q: Chiang Mai was the capital of which kingdom?

Q986198.t: Auckland's southern side, on a vast tidal harbour
Q986198.s: Twice a day the Manukau Harbour nearly empties: at low tide, great sheets of mudflats and winding channels shine where there was water a few hours before. This huge, shallow harbour opens west to the Tasman Sea, and along its shore spreads Manukau, once a city in its own right and since 2010 part of Auckland. Auckland Airport's runway runs along the water's edge.
Q986198.w: Suburbs on the shore of a huge, shallow harbour with mudflats and channels, an airport runway along the water's edge.
f: On the Tāmaki isthmus, Māori once dragged canoes overland between the Manukau and the Pacific side, a gap of barely a kilometre.
Small volcanic cones of the Auckland volcanic field, such as Māngere Mountain, rise near the harbour.
The Manukau is New Zealand's second-largest natural harbour.

q.q: Which body of water does the Manukau Harbour open onto?

Q14525.t: A town near the equator, between a gulf and a lake
Q14525.s: Less than 70 km north of the equator, Gorontalo fills a flat valley on the northern arm of Sulawesi, where a river reaches the calm Gulf of Tomini. Just west spreads Lake Limboto, a broad, shallow lake that has shrunk as silt fills it. And off the beach at Botubarani, a short way east of town, whale sharks often feed close to shore.
Q14525.w: A town in a flat valley on the Gulf of Tomini, with a broad, shallow lake just to the west.
f: The Gulf of Tomini is almost entirely enclosed by the long arms of Sulawesi.
On a hill above the lake stands Otanaha, a small fort traditionally dated to the 16th century.

q.q: Which gulf does Gorontalo face?

Q696605.t: Gateway to Mohenjo-daro on the Indus plain
Q696605.s: About 25 km south of Larkana, near a bend of the Indus, lie the brick ruins of Mohenjo-daro, one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilisation, built more than 4,500 years ago. Larkana itself stands on the flat, irrigated right bank of the river, among rice fields and canals. Far to the west, the Kirthar Range rises as a bare brown wall.
Q696605.w: A town on a flat, green plain of rice fields and canals west of the Indus, with bare mountains far to the west.
f: Mohenjo-daro became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1980.
Its streets were laid out on a grid, with covered drains and a great public bath.

q.q: Which ancient Indus city lies near Larkana?

Q760714.t: Silk City on the Ganges, with dolphins in the river
Q760714.s: The Ganges runs wide and braided past Bhagalpur, and in this stretch lives one of the world's rarest river animals: the nearly blind Ganges river dolphin, protected in the Vikramshila sanctuary. The city itself is India's Silk City, famous for tussar silk with a natural golden sheen. About 50 km east lie the ruins of Vikramashila, a great Buddhist university of the Pala kings.
Q760714.w: A city on the south bank of a wide, braided river with sandbars, green farmland on both sides.
f: The Ganges river dolphin is almost blind and finds its way by echolocation.
Vikramashila was founded around 800 CE by the Pala king Dharmapala.

q.q: Which rare animal is protected in the Ganges at Bhagalpur?

Q486545.t: An ancient Silk Road oasis below the Kyrgyz range
Q486545.s: Where the Talas River comes down from the mountains onto the steppe, Taraz spreads out in a green oasis, with the snowy Kyrgyz Alatau on the southern horizon. The town was already a Silk Road trading post in the 6th century, visited by a Byzantine embassy in 568. Nearby, in 751, Arab and Chinese armies fought the Battle of Talas, which set the limits of Tang China's power in Central Asia.
Q486545.w: A green oasis city on a river where the mountains meet the steppe, with a snowy range along the southern horizon.
f: The Aisha Bibi mausoleum near Taraz is faced with carved terracotta tiles in dozens of patterns.
Taraz celebrated its 2,000th anniversary in 2002.

q.q: Near Taraz in 751, Arab armies fought troops of which empire?
